source_snapshot.procedure: Use BMC Web Operations -> Reboot BMC, observe management-IP disconnection during reboot, then reconnection with working BMC functions.
source_snapshot.criteria: Management connectivity is lost during reboot and returns with usable BMC functions.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; substitutes IPMI cold reset or Redfish Manager.Reset and checks return after about 60 seconds.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION/HIGH; preserve the WebUI control path, use independent observation, staged readiness checks, bounded timeouts, host invariance and no retry.

old_problem: The source named a WebUI operation but DeepSeek replaced it with IPMI/Redfish reset, and neither defined the outage/readiness timeline, full BMC function matrix, critical-task exclusion, independent recovery channel or host-state invariance.
disposition_reason: The engineering method is fully defined once runtime BMC identity, WebUI labels and approved timing values are supplied. ED-03 permits those build-specific values as configuration; ED-08 requires actual WebUI visual/action evidence, so API resets may observe readiness but do not replace the Operations-page stimulus unless the project explicitly changes coverage. A BMC reboot has clear phased observables—session loss, network return, fresh authentication, IPMI/Redfish/WebUI/provider readiness and final function checks—and an independent recovery/no-retry policy can be specified without another design decision. Pending is therefore removed while execution still requires outage authorization.
decision_basis: Directly read XLSX Functionality rows 2282 and 2283 with row-2282 Items, Procedure, Criteria and DeepSeek fields; row 2283 is the verified next formal pending identity.
Read GPT V2/historical record 2403 and retained the exact Source Key, Variant ID and source-row hash.
Preserve the source's actual BMC Web Operations control, observed disconnect, reconnect and restored-function coverage.
Distinguish network reachability from application readiness; ping alone is not sufficient.
ED-11/ED-12 require a one-shot action with no automatic reset retry, and host power/workload state must remain invariant.
No browser action, BMC reset, service outage or DUT query occurred.

test_case.test_name: BMC Web Operations reboot with complete management-service recovery
test_case.purpose: Verify the exact authenticated BMC Web Operations/Reboot BMC control initiates one management-controller reboot, causes the expected bounded management outage and restores all required BMC functions without changing host power or workload state.
required_package: Exact BMC target, firmware/WebUI/browser build and Operations/Reboot control mapping
Authorized outage window, credentials/TLS policy and WebUI capture method
Signed onset, network, authentication, IPMI, Redfish, WebUI/provider and full-readiness timeouts
No-critical-task checklist and post-reboot BMC function matrix
Independent console/observer and approved timeout recovery plan
test_case.test_command: Capture BMC identity, host state, active update/recovery/tasks, services and existing logs. After explicit outage approval, use the authenticated BMC Web interface to navigate to Operations and activate Reboot BMC exactly once while an independent observer timestamps browser/session loss, network loss/return, fresh authentication, IPMI, Redfish, sensor provider and WebUI recovery. Run the approved final BMC function checklist and compare host power/workload state with baseline.
test_case.expected_result: The WebUI action is visibly accepted once; management access becomes unavailable within the approved onset window, returns through each readiness phase within its deadline, all required BMC functions pass with correct identity, and host power/workload state remains unchanged without unexplained critical events.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires real evidence of the Web Operations action, observed outage, staged service recovery within signed timeouts, complete function checklist and host-state invariance. An IPMI/Redfish-triggered reset without approved equivalence, ping-only return, cached session, missing Web evidence, repeated reset or host power impact is not PASS. The end engineer decides PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED.
safety_gate: Confirm no firmware update, recovery, log export, critical management task or sole-dependent workload is active.
Use an independent observer/recovery path because the initiating Web session is expected to disappear.
Issue one reboot only and preserve existing logs/events rather than clearing them.
Stop on identity change, repeated flapping, host impact or any readiness timeout; do not retry or power-cycle automatically.
Require a new authorization if target, command path, outage window or recovery method changes.
expected_evidence: Row/variant/hash, BMC/WebUI/browser identity and outage authorization
Screenshots/video or equivalent visual evidence of exact Operations/Reboot action and confirmation
Host-state comparison, alternate-recovery status and engineer-owned verdict
test_case.recovery: On a readiness timeout or flapping service, do not send another reset. Preserve browser, network, console and service traces; use the approved independent management/service-console recovery once and escalate to the BMC owner before any host power action.

source_conflict.reason: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently require a WebUI-triggered reboot with outage and restored function; API substitution was an AI-review mismatch, not protected-source conflict.

blocked.reason: The Web action, observation method, safety gates and recovery are defined. Build-specific labels and timeouts are runtime configuration.
